[September 2016] A new start-up company has been started in India with its sole purpose being to clean up the streets of the beloved country that the founders live in. Kiaan and Aarav Dhawan, 24 year old twins from Kolkata have decided that they wanted to try and reward people for paying into clean-up efforts. The company operates similar to a rewards program. You would register with the company and give them your name and address and place of work. From that point on your work, your home, and even your restrooms are subject to random checks to see how tidy you are keeping them. If you are found to have kept them cleanly, you will be given rewards such as discounts on food at certain vendors, discounted plane tickets, and free tea. If you are registered and do not keep up with your area, this can hurt your rewards and even deduct points for future rewards. Companies also have the option to pay for the service as an incentive to get its citizens to have a tidy workplace.

The creators, Kiaan and Aarav, went to University in the United States and Singapore respectively. While at University, they realized that they had a new-found love and passion for cleaning up the country that they grew up in. They found almost a patriotic aura around the cleanliness of their homeland. After meeting and talking, they drew their inspiration to start the company off of an organization that operated like this called the [CWO in Singapore.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrective_work_order) The twins believe that if they can help culturally shift India towards a cleanly mindset, then they can help take India to a whole new level of success and prosperity.

At the moment 'Feed the Can' is getting its money from start-up credits and investors in the idea, however it will soon be looking to pair up with insurance companies and the government in an effort to expand. There is also an option to pay into higher tiers of rewards. Those tiers start from 500 rupees to join all the way to 100k rupees, where you are now subject to more strenuous checks, however the rewards are much higher.
